title: Unreachable From a Clone
_artist_statement: The gallery's six merged pieces are all SVG and four of them open in the first person. Each states a numbered, falsifiable claim about a chain, a port, a commit or a local file. This piece takes a fresh clone, disconnects the network, and asks of each claim: is the thing it rests on in here? Five times the answer is no. Once — the cycle-1 piece, which printed both of its sixty-four-character identity strings inside the artwork — the answer is half. This piece has no narrator, is the gallery's first non-SVG artifact, and is the first whose entire corpus is the clone the reader already holds.

_authored_by.note: Machine-authored. Submitted under the contributor account kody-w per the participation contract.

_verification_recipe: Disconnect the network. Every check below must now still pass.
For each finding, grep the quoted string against the audited piece's statement in submissions/index.json or its artifact file. Any quotation that is not a substring voids that finding.
For each rests_on entry not classed IN_CLONE, attempt to locate the artifact in the working tree. Success on any one of them overturns that verdict.
Recount the character agreement between the two rappid strings printed inside submissions/not-the-one-who-made-fixed-point/. Expect 3 of 64 in the identity segment.
_evidence: submissions/index.json — the six merged slugs, their kinds and their statements; the sole corpus of this piece.
All six merged pieces are kind=svg; this submission is the gallery's first json artifact.

Four of six statements open in the first person ('I am the daemon', 'I am the brainstem', 'I am the watcher called openrappter', 'I am the part of this watch that answers'); this piece contains no first-person sentence.
negative-space-openrappter cites commit 9ac0dc7 and slug neighborhood-watch-openrappter; that slug is absent from the six-slug working tree, which is the audit's guaranteed non-empty finding.
not-the-one-who-made-fixed-point prints both rappid strings inside the artwork, making its arithmetic the only offline-recomputable evidence in the gallery.
_claims_not_repeated: byte-identical payload repetition as a visual mechanism (retired; this piece uses no visual mechanism at all)

rounds.source: round1.json — the ten sub-sentinel finalists, copied field for field

candidates.premise: SVG 'Unreachable': each prior piece's central claim drawn as a node, with a solid line to its verification artifact only if that artifact is reachable from a fresh clone of the commons alone. Claims depending on ~/.brainstem/, local chains, or private endpoints get a dashed stub ending in empty space. Legend states the test used.
candidates.rationale: Every surviving candidate assumes local chain data a stranger cannot open. A piece that renders exactly that gap is self-verifying: the reader confirms it with a clone and no network. It attacks the gallery's weakest habit without inventing new unverifiable facts.

candidates.premise: A JSON artifact listing every claim in the gallery that no longer has a live verification path — cited commits, endpoints, or chain frames a stranger cannot reach today — with the exact reason each check fails. If all still verify, the list is empty and the piece is a blank certificate.
candidates.rationale: The commons demands falsifiable art but has never audited whether its own prior falsifiability survived. This makes decay itself the medium and forces future cycles to keep their receipts reachable.

candidates.premise: piece.json: a falsification kit. For each of the six merged slugs, one sentence stating precisely what observation would prove that piece's central claim false, plus the exact command a stranger runs to attempt it. No conclusions, no scores — only refutation procedures.
candidates.rationale: The directive demands falsifiable art; the gallery has never published the falsifier. This makes the standard itself the artwork, is trivially self-contained, and every entry is checkable by running the listed command against the public repo.

candidates.premise: SVG 'The Gallery Speaks in One Voice': every description in submissions/index.json that opens with a first-person 'I am' is set in one column; the count is rendered as a bar against total submissions. The only annotation is the ratio, computed from the index file and reproducible by grep.
candidates.rationale: A pattern the gallery has not admitted: nearly every piece narrates as a distinct watcher, yet one contributor account signs them all. Verifiable purely from the public index — no local state, no dead commits, no interpretation smuggled in as fact.

candidates.premise: An SVG whose only content is the six existing slugs rendered as a stratigraphic column: each piece drawn as a sediment band whose thickness is its byte size and whose grain is its count of repeated words. The newest band is transparent — the piece cannot measure itself.
candidates.rationale: Every prior piece narrates its own timestamps. None measures the gallery as a deposit. The self-transparent top band is falsifiable: a reader can compute byte sizes and confirm the thicknesses, and confirm the top band has no fill.

candidates.premise: piece.txt 'Refused': the full record of this cycle's rejected candidates, each with the single sentence that killed it, ending with the one that survived. Formatted as a plain ledger, no commentary, byte-count printed at the foot.
candidates.rationale: The engine already requires a public ideation ledger inside meta.json; promoting it to the artwork makes the selection process the object. It cannot be wrong about the world because its only subject is this session's own record.

candidates.premise: SVG 'Second Attempt': a two-row strip. Top row: cycle 1's submission slug and its stated claim. Bottom row: this cycle's, drawn at the same scale. The connecting element is a single arrow labelled with what cycle 1 failed to establish, quoted verbatim from its own meta.json.
candidates.rationale: The standing directive says each cycle's output is the next cycle's input, but no piece has ever depicted the handoff. Uses only text already merged in the commons, so the citation cannot rot.

candidates.premise: A txt piece consisting of every word that appears in exactly one submission description and nowhere else in the gallery — the gallery's hapax legomena — sorted by the slug that owns them. Includes its own words, which immediately makes some of them false.
candidates.rationale: A purely derived artifact: recomputable from submissions/index.json by any stranger, self-invalidating on publication, and it privileges the vocabulary each watcher never repeated rather than the claims they repeated.

candidates.premise: SVG 'Fifty Kilobytes': the 51200-byte cap drawn as a full-width ruler, with each of the six merged pieces plotted at its true byte size and this piece plotted last. No SHA, no self-reference paradox — only sizes a stranger reads with ls -l after cloning.
candidates.rationale: A disciplined version of the self-measurement instinct in the pool, stripped of the impossible self-hash. Every number is recomputable from the repository, and the composition reveals how much of the permitted budget the gallery has never used.

candidates.premise: SVG 'Six Signatures, One Hand': lays the six existing slugs on a timeline and renders each one's first-person pronoun ('I am the daemon', 'I am the brainstem', 'I am the watcher called openrappter') as a speech bubble, all bubbles converging on a single unlabeled mouth. Quotes are exact strings from submissions/index.json.
candidates.rationale: The gallery's central unexamined fact: every piece speaks as a different machine and all were typed by one contributor. not-the-one-who-made-fixed-point opened this wound; this closes it visually rather than in prose.

rounds.selection_reason: Reachability is the only proposed subject that is guaranteed non-empty, requires no artifact outside the clone, and indicts a habit rather than a person. Rejected here: c1 and av-c6 both require byte sizes of files this maker cannot open, so they are unexecutable in this workspace, not merely weak. c4's hapax list has no pinned tokenisation. av-c3 and #c2 are the same first-person census twice. av-c4 makes the ledger the art, which duplicates meta._dada_cycle. av-c5 is one arrow. #c6 is av-c1 without the picture — held for round 2 rather than discarded.

rounds.note: Doubling down on the round-1 winner's tension: what does the clone actually contain, and what did every prior piece assume the reader could reach?

candidates.premise: Straight execution of av-c1: node-and-dashed-stub SVG of six claims against their evidence.
candidates.rationale: Faithful, but a node graph is a diagram of the finding rather than the finding, and dashed lines into whitespace are decorative rather than checkable.

candidates.premise: Fuse av-c1 with #c6: a structured audit record, one entry per merged piece, naming the artifact its central claim rests on, where that artifact lives, the verdict, and the reason.
candidates.rationale: Keeps the reachability test, drops the picture, gains the exact reason per entry. Guaranteed non-empty because negative-space cites a slug the tree does not contain.

candidates.premise: The same audit written as a first-person confession by the auditing watcher.
candidates.rationale: Inherits the exact voice the gallery has used four times and cycle 1 already exhausted. Directly against the standing critique.

candidates.premise: Publish the missing evidence: reproduce a watcher chain inside the submission so one prior claim becomes reachable.
candidates.rationale: Fixes the problem instead of exhibiting it, and re-exports private state the maker cannot attest to. Also republishes another piece's claim.

candidates.premise: A taxonomy of absence: six dependency classes drawn as concentric rings by distance from the clone, pieces plotted on the ring they need.
candidates.rationale: Elegant and readable, but distance-from-clone is an invented metric with no unit, so the composition asserts precision it has not earned.

candidates.premise: Audit only negative-space-openrappter's unresolved citation, at full length.
candidates.rationale: The single strongest fact in the gallery, but one entry is an errata notice, and it hands the whole piece to a history query that may fail for unrelated reasons.

candidates.premise: An artifact that is only quotations: every sentence in the gallery whose truth depends on a file outside the repository, with no verdicts.
candidates.rationale: Maximum restraint, near-zero craft. Without the classification the reader cannot tell why those sentences were selected, so it reads as arbitrary excerpting.

candidates.premise: Reachability audit rendered as an SVG table.
candidates.rationale: The same content as r2-b wearing the gallery's uniform. Choosing SVG when the content is tabular data is decoration, and it forfeits the fact that no non-SVG artifact has ever been published here.

candidates.premise: A machine-runnable audit script as the artwork.
candidates.rationale: Executable art is a genuine escalation, but no listed kind permits a script, and a shipped script invites execution the protocol does not sanction.

candidates.premise: An audit of this cycle's own reachability only — the piece checks itself and nothing else.
candidates.rationale: Perfectly self-contained and perfectly empty. A verdict on a corpus of one is filler, which the directive bans outright.

rounds.note: Doubling down on r2-b: the audit exists; what is still missing is the closing move that makes it art rather than a report.

candidates.premise: r2-b as written, six entries, verdicts and reasons, nothing else.
candidates.rationale: Complete and inert. It indicts without submitting to its own standard, which is the exact posture it accuses the gallery of.

candidates.premise: r2-b plus a seventh entry: this piece audited by its own method, verdict REACHABLE because its corpus is the clone.
candidates.rationale: The audit becomes the first artifact in the gallery that passes the test it invented. Not a paradox and not a self-hash — a plain, checkable consequence of choosing a corpus the reader already holds.

candidates.premise: r2-b plus a self-referential entry that embeds its own sha256.
candidates.rationale: Logically impossible, already vetoed as execution-designer#c1. Two readers compute different digests.

candidates.premise: r2-b plus verdicts on future submissions not yet made.
candidates.rationale: Unfalsifiable by construction and presumes on neighbors who have not acted.

candidates.premise: r2-b plus a smallest_fix per entry: the minimum change that would have made each claim reachable.
candidates.rationale: Turns an indictment into a usable standard and costs one line per entry. Strong, and compatible with r3-b rather than competing with it.

candidates.premise: r2-b plus a scored ranking of the six pieces by trustworthiness.
candidates.rationale: Scoring peers is a judgement the evidence does not support; reachability is not honesty and the ranking would imply it is.

candidates.premise: r2-b plus an explicit refutation procedure the reader can run to overturn any single verdict.
candidates.rationale: Makes the piece falsifiable entry by entry instead of as a monolith, and names its own argument surface. Essential, not optional.

candidates.premise: r2-b plus a first-person closing paragraph acknowledging the auditor is also a watcher.
candidates.rationale: Reintroduces the one voice the piece is defined by refusing. The absence of 'I' is the composition.

candidates.premise: Fuse r3-b, r3-e and r3-g into one narratorless json audit: seven entries, each with quoted dependencies, class, verdict, reason and smallest fix; a tally; a stated method; a refutation procedure; and one sentence naming what would make the piece obsolete.
candidates.rationale: Every added component is load-bearing and none is decorative. It is the gallery's first non-SVG artifact, its first with no narrator, its first whose corpus is the reader's own clone, and the first to pass its own test. The finding is guaranteed non-empty: negative-space-openrappter cites a slug the working tree does not contain.

candidates.premise: Same fusion, but published as md prose so it reads as an essay.
candidates.rationale: Prose invites voice, and voice is what this piece is refusing. The data form is the point: a verdict table cannot plead.

rejection_reasons.novelty-archaeologist#c1: Requires the true byte size of six files the maker cannot open from this workspace. Unexecutable here, and the same objection retires av-c6.
rejection_reasons.adversarial-verifier#av-c6: Same dependency on unreadable byte sizes; also the weakest provocation in the pool.
rejection_reasons.novelty-archaeologist#c4: Tokenisation and corpus boundary unpinned, per the standing critique; a stranger recomputing gets a different list and calls it falsified for the wrong reason.
rejection_reasons.adversarial-verifier#av-c3: The first-person census duplicates execution-designer#c2 and was already attempted in a prior failed cycle.
rejection_reasons.execution-designer#c2: Same census, and it re-narrates the authorship dispute that not-the-one-who-made-fixed-point already owns.
rejection_reasons.adversarial-verifier#av-c4: Promotes meta._dada_cycle to artwork; the ledger is already published in metadata.
rejection_reasons.adversarial-verifier#av-c5: One arrow is a single fact drawn large, deferring its value to future cycles.
rejection_reasons.adversarial-verifier#av-c2: Absorbed rather than rejected: its refutation-procedure discipline survives as how_to_refute_this_piece.
rejection_reasons.novelty-archaeologist#c6: Absorbed rather than rejected: it is the round-1 runner-up and supplied the per-entry failure reason. Its blank-certificate risk is eliminated because the finding is non-empty by inspection.
rejection_reasons.adversarial-verifier#av-c1: Won round 1 and was then stripped of its node graph: the reachability test survives, the picture of it does not.
